newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power rallies with natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power rallies with natgas.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. rallied Monday in tandem with a sharp rise in natural gas prices, and helped by return of winter-like temperatures in the region.
Latest forecasts showed a cold front has pushed out a mild weather system that hovered over the midsection of the Atlantic seaboard last week.

Temperatures in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district Tuesday would peak in 20-40 degrees Fahrenheit during the day and bottom in the teens and 30s at night, down 10-20 degrees from last week.
Tuesday PJM power, excluding transmission costs, for firm, peak delivery jumped roughly seven dollars to $25.50-$26.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), from Friday's $19.00-$21.00 for Monday.
Tuesday, peak, firm trades reportedly changed hands in a $25.00-$27.50 range.
Firm, off-peak PJM electricity for Tuesday delivery was notionally valued at $16.00-$18.00, up from Friday's $15.00-$16.00 range.
PJM power deliveries for the rest of January with similar delivery terms was quoted near $29.00, up from $26.75-$27.75 Friday.
February PJM electricity was valued at $30.50-$30.80 after traded as high as $31.00. The quote was stronger than Friday's $28.90-$29.40.
March PJM electricity rose about a dollar to $25.40-$25.80 from $24.25-$24.50 Friday.
PJM electricity prices for April and May edged up to $22.60-$23.10 from Friday's $22.50-22.70.
July/August PJM deliveries were quoted at $31.60-$31.80 with reported trades at $31.85, firmer than $31.30-$31.80 Friday.
The natural gas market surged today on forecast of cold weather in the Midwest and news of a weekend outage at the 1,150 megawatt (MW) Comanche Peak nuclear unit 2 in Texas.
Swing gas deliveries to the Philadelphia city gate were traded in a $3.80-$4.00 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range up from Friday's $3.50.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures rocketed up 61.9 cents/mmBtu to $3.725.
PECO Energy Co's 1,055 MW Limerick unit 2 would hold production in the 80 percent range ahead of its refueling outage scheduled to begin January 31.
